search.nav.label: Search sections
search.off.title: Search is switched off
search.off.body: This shop does not use the search engine (SEARCH_ENABLED is false). The storefront lists products from the catalog, and the search status, rebuild and synonyms have nothing to show.
search.off.step1: Run Meilisearch and create an API key scoped to the index prefix (README, Catalog search).
search.off.step2: Set SEARCH_ENABLED=true, MEILI_URL and MEILI_API_KEY in the API environment, and restart the API.
search.off.step3: Build the indexes once with pnpm search:reindex, or request a rebuild on the Status screen.
search.off.secretNote: The key belongs in the server environment only: it is never entered or shown in this admin.
search.status.intro: Where the search index stands: the engine, the index of each language and the queue of catalog changes waiting to be sent to it.
search.engine.title: Search engine
search.engine.unreachableNote: Searches on the storefront fall back to the catalog list until it answers again. Catalog changes wait in the queue.
search.engine.code.engine_unreachable: The API cannot connect to the engine. Check that it is running and that MEILI_URL is right.
search.engine.code.engine_timeout: The engine did not answer in time.
search.engine.code.engine_unauthorized: The engine refused the API key. Check MEILI_API_KEY and its scope.
search.engine.code.engine_index_missing: An index the API needs does not exist yet. Request a rebuild.
search.engine.code.engine_rejected: The engine refused a request of the API. This is a bug or a drift between the API and the index settings; check the API log.
search.engine.code.engine_unavailable: The engine reports a server error or is overloaded.
search.engine.code.engine_bad_response: The engine sent an answer the API could not read.
search.engine.code.engine_task_failed: The engine accepted a change but failed to apply it.
search.engine.code.engine_task_timeout: The engine took too long to apply a change.
search.engine.code.unrecognized: A failure with a code this screen does not know.
search.rejected.title: Searches refused by the engine
search.rejected.body: Refused since the API started: {count}. The engine refused these searches (a bug or a drift between the API and the index settings, not an outage); each shopper saw an error. The count starts again when the API restarts.
search.rejected.none: The engine has refused no search since the API started.
search.lane.title: Store search capacity
search.lane.intro: Store searches and suggestions share a limited number of engine slots per API process; each search takes the slots of all its parallel engine calls at once. Counted by this API process since {time}; the numbers start again when the API restarts.
search.lane.noneRefused: No search was turned away for lack of capacity.
search.lane.refusedTitle: Searches turned away for lack of capacity
search.lane.refusedBody: Turned away: {count} ({share} of the searches asked for). Those shoppers saw the catalog listing instead of search results.
search.lane.advice: If the search engine has spare processor capacity, raise SEARCH_ENGINE_MAX_CONCURRENCY and restart the API; if it is already fully busy, give it more processors first.
search.lane.abandoned: Left while waiting (the shopper's connection closed first)
search.lane.refusedWaitExceeded: Turned away: waited longer than 1 second
search.indexes.title: Indexes
search.indexes.intro: One index per language, built from the published catalog. Changes reach it through the sync queue; a rebuild builds a new index and swaps it in.
search.stateHelp.building: A new index is being built and will be swapped in when it is complete. Searches use the current index meanwhile.
search.stateHelp.never_indexed: There is no index for this language yet, so storefront searches fall back to the catalog list. Request a rebuild.
search.stateHelp.rebuild_requested: A rebuild was requested and waits for the next run of the rebuild job.
search.stateHelp.documents_stale: The index was built for an older document format or another shop currency. A rebuild is due and the job will start it.
search.stateHelp.settings_pending: A synonym or catalog definition change waits for the next sync, which applies it in place without a rebuild.
search.stateHelp.fresh: The index has the current documents and settings.
search.localeError.title: The last sync failed
search.queue.title: Sync queue
search.queue.intro: Catalog changes wait here until the sync job sends them to the engine.
search.queue.state.empty: Nothing is waiting: the index is in step with the catalog.
search.queue.state.draining: Changes are waiting for the next sync.
search.queue.state.attention: Some products keep failing. They are tried again every hour; check the codes below and the API log.
search.queue.noErrorsBody: No product in the queue has a failed attempt.
search.rebuild.title: Rebuild the index
search.rebuild.body: Builds a new index for every language from the database and swaps it in when it is complete; searches keep using the current index meanwhile. It is rarely needed: catalog changes reach the index through the queue. The rebuild job starts it at its next run.
search.rebuild.readOnly: You can read the search status. Requesting a rebuild needs permission to change the catalog.
search.rebuild.confirmBody: A rebuild is requested for every language. It runs in the background, can take a while on a large catalog and loads the engine. Searches keep working with the current index.
search.rebuild.requestedNote: Nothing has been rebuilt yet: each language shows "Rebuild requested" until the new index is swapped in. Asking again changes nothing while a build runs.
search.rebuild.off: Search is switched off (SEARCH_ENABLED is false): there is nothing to rebuild.
search.rebuild.forbidden: You are not allowed to request a rebuild.
search.rebuild.unknownBody: The answer was lost, so the request may or may not have been recorded. The status above is read again: a language that shows "Rebuild requested" has it. The request is not sent again automatically.
search.synonyms.intro: Groups of words that find each other, per language: a shopper who types any word of a group also finds products that match the others (for example "викрутка" and "відвертка"). Terms are lower-cased and cleaned like a search query.
search.synonyms.applyNote: A change reaches the search index with the next sync (usually within a minute or two) and needs no rebuild.
search.synonyms.queueNow: Products waiting in the sync queue now: {depth}.
search.synonyms.readOnly: You can read the synonym groups. Changing them needs permission to change the catalog.
search.synonyms.caption: Synonym groups
search.synonyms.emptyBody: Add a group so that shoppers who type one word also find products described with another.
search.synonyms.emptyLocaleBody: This language has no synonym groups. Add one, or choose another language.
search.synonyms.pastEnd: There are no groups on this page.
search.synonyms.formDescription: The terms find each other in both directions.
search.synonyms.termsHint: Separate the terms with commas or line breaks. {min} to {max} different terms, each at most {maxWords} words and {maxLength} characters.
search.synonyms.deleteBody: Delete the group "{terms}" ({locale})? Once the next sync has run, shoppers who type one of these words no longer find products by the others.
search.synonyms.dialogOff: Search is switched off (SEARCH_ENABLED is false), so nothing can be saved.
search.synonyms.dialogForbidden: You are not allowed to change synonym groups.
search.synonyms.issue.unusable: These have no letters or digits left, or contain control characters: {terms}.
search.synonyms.error.not_a_list: The terms were not sent as a list.
search.synonyms.error.too_few_terms: A group needs at least two different terms.
search.synonyms.error.too_many_terms: A group has at most 20 terms.
search.synonyms.error.invalid_term: A term is not allowed: at most 3 words and 50 characters, with letters or digits and no control characters.
search.synonyms.error.duplicate_terms: Two terms are the same once cleaned (case and spacing do not count).
search.synonyms.notice.appliesLater: It reaches the search index with the next sync.
search.synonyms.notice.unchanged: The terms are the same as before, so nothing was sent.
search.synonyms.notice.gone: That group no longer exists (someone else may have deleted it). The list was read again.
search.synonyms.notice.unknown.create: The answer was lost, so the group may or may not have been added. The list was read again: check it before adding the group a second time.
search.synonyms.notice.unknown.update: The answer was lost, so the change may or may not have been saved. The list was read again: check the terms before changing them a second time.
search.synonyms.notice.unknown.delete: The answer was lost, so the group may or may not have been deleted. The list was read again.
